summary: The team is in a critical push to launch the Intelligent China webpage this week while managing a wave of post-Tech in Asia Conference follow-ups and finalizing the knowledge website redesign.
summaryDetail: The top priority is the Intelligent China program: the webpage must go live this week to start driving traffic, with Module 1 prioritized for marketing and sales, and Joseph tasked to create three tabs with separate URLs for each module. In parallel, the team is executing follow-up from the Tech in Asia Conference: sending a combined appreciation and program information email to participants, creating touch points, and adding upcoming program lists to the follow-up email. The knowledge website redesign is nearing completion, with decisions to combine design elements, remove the video section, and keep the two-menu structure; Joseph needs to share the HTML file and the team must meet to mark specific feedback. Urgent this week: resolve the Outlook account lockout by deleting and re-adding accounts on all devices, and contact JSB to confirm the backend unlock. Looking ahead, the team must analyze existing participant profiles, audit conversion tracking, and prepare October work priorities for website, SEM/SEO, GEO, and content, while also finalizing the Asia Start spotlight article and video timeline.

meetings.title: Knowledge Website Design Review
meetings.summary: The team reviewed two design versions for the knowledge website, comparing the current layout with Joseph's more editorial-inspired version. They agreed the current design is largely similar to the proposed one, with the main change being menu categorization, and decided to combine elements from both versions while removing the outdated video section.

meetings.summary: The team discussed prioritizing promotion of Asia Star and Intelligent China programs, with a secondary focus on Berkeley, and reviewed conversion tracking setup to ensure accurate measurement.
